get.description:
Constants compiled into the binary: the neck's logical pitch/yaw envelope,                       home pose and velocity ceilings; the torso lift's stroke; the mobile base's                       speed ceilings and watchdog intervals; the arm's                       per-joint travel, both arms' HOME pose (`arm.home_deg`, degrees, the kit's pose) and both arms' STOW pose (`arm.stow_deg`, degrees, the kit's storage pose).

No device is touched, so this answers on a robot with                       everything asleep or soft-killed — which is the point: a consumer clamps to                       these before a command is ever sent. Anything that varies per robot or per                       moment is device STATE and lives under `*/state` instead. The neck figures                       are the LOGICAL frame (`neck/cmd`'s frame, pitch positive = up); the motor                       frame beneath it is this daemon's business and is deliberately not                       published.

The `arm_feedback.shm/1` record as JSON: the newest controller feedback record the daemon received (about one per millisecond while the controller streams), with both arms' state, error and frame-miss counters, measured, echoed and accepted joint commands, velocity, position error, current, torque, temperature, the controller's friction, force and Cartesian-force estimates, the impedance, force-control and tool registrations in effect, the parameter-reply slot, and the 1428-byte record itself (base64). The fields are the contract's, under its names, in the controller's own units and codes; `header.seq` counts the records since the daemon started and `rx_mono_ns` is `CLOCK_MONOTONIC` at receipt, so a record can be lined up with the same record read from shared memory or pushed by the `arm.feedback` subscription. `layout_sha256` is the contract's layout pin. A daemon whose arm backend streams no records, or that has received none yet, answers unavailable.
get.summary: Read the newest arm controller feedback record, both arms, every signal

get.description: One entry per arm side, `a` then `b`, each the same object `/v1/end_effectors/{side}` answers: whether the side is fitted, what its driver declares (`descriptor`: driver, model, the bus address the startup probe found, joints with units and limits, capabilities, the tool model registered on the arm) and its state (openness estimate, joints, contact, cap reached, the driver's own report under `detail`). A side whose read failed carries `state: null` and the reason in `error`; the list itself never fails.

A direct read of the slider controller over its serial link (about 100-200 ms). An unreadable slider is an error envelope (`502`), unlike the `/v1/state` slot which degrades in place.

The lift's limits are published by SIDE, because the two sides may legitimately hold different values and neither is derived from the other. `travel_limits` is the SOFTWARE side, which this daemon records and checks: every layer and the `effective` range they come to together, which is the range `set_height` admits; `model` is `[0, travel_max_m]` from the daemon's configuration, and `unit` is this robot's bench calibration (written by `slider/set_limits`) or `null` when none has been recorded. A layer only ever narrows. `hardware_limits` is the HARDWARE side, which the drive holds and enforces by itself, read back from the drive: its position-limit registers (`0x6006`-`0x6009`), whether they are in force (`Pr8.00` bit 1), and its origin settings. When both sides are set and differ, `advisory` says so (`slider_limits_differ`), naming both values.

`alarm`, `alarm_code` and `alarm_text` are the drive's alarm register. A carriage stepped into its mechanical bottom stalls there and the drive raises an alarm and takes no further motion until `slider/reset_alarm`; which code the D1's drive raises for that stall has not been recorded, so read the alarm rather than matching a code. `multiturn_lost` is `true` while the alarm is Er153 (`0x153`, decimal 339), the multi-turn encoder's battery error: the absolute position is lost. `slider/reset_alarm` does not clear it; `slider/set_zero` recovers it before it sets the zero.

`zero_verification` is separate from `zero_reference` and additive to it. `zero_reference` asks whether the drive can vouch for its origin right now; this asks whether the origin this daemon last wrote has been read back after a power cycle, which is the only evidence that the drive persisted it rather than holding it in RAM. `unrecorded` means this daemon has no record of setting one and is not a fault.

`advisory` is additive and absent unless the origin, or two sides holding different limits, earn one; a commissioned and verified lift whose two sides agree never carries one. Nothing on the advisory path writes to the drive.

The localization strategy, its graded state (`lost`, `converging`, `confident`) with its score and spreads, and the pose. Forwarded to `d1-amr-firmwared`, the daemon of the in-house base firmware, which `d1-firmwared` reaches only under `[chassis] backend = "d1amr"`; under any other chassis backend the operation answers 502 `unavailable`. The request and response bodies are those of `d1-amr-firmwared`, defined by d1-amr-firmware's contract (its `interfaces/openapi.json`) and not restated in this document: `data` is that daemon's answer, unchanged, and its refusal arrives as this API's error envelope with its `reason_code` in the message.

data.description: A JSON value forwarded from the chassis vendor; its shape is not pinned by this document.

get.description: `null` when the arms are free, including when the last lease has expired but nobody has taken it since. The same reading appears as `arm.lease` in `/v1/state`.

post.description:
Arbitration between the consumers that can all reach this daemon — a teleop session, a policy, and the robot's own ambient motion. While a lease is held, arm motion from anyone else is refused with 409 naming the holder; reads, `estop`, `clear_errors`, `recover` and the soft kill are never arbitrated.

Granted when the lease is free, when the current one has expired, or when you already hold it — that last case is the heartbeat, so renew by repeating this call well inside `ttl_s`. `ttl_s` defaults to 30 seconds and may not exceed 600; expiry is evaluated when the lease is next read, so a consumer that dies frees the arms without anything having to notice it died.

**Priority.** `class` is `ambient` (rank 10), `policy` (50) or `operator` (90), and **an omitted `class` means `ambient`** — the lowest privilege there is, so a consumer written before classes existed cannot outrank one written after. A request of a strictly HIGHER class than the holder preempts it: the answer carries `preempted_from` and a new `epoch`. An equal class is first-come (409), and a lower one is 409 too. `epoch` increments on every fresh grant and never on a heartbeat, so a consumer that reads its own name back can tell "I still hold these" from "I lost them and have them again" — and therefore whether what it believed about the arms is stale.

**A preemption stops the arms first.** The displaced holder's trajectory is cancelled (`cancelled`, not `failed`) and both arms are taken exclusively before the grant is recorded, so the new holder never inherits a moving robot. The arm mode is deliberately NOT changed: a position or torque hold is where the arms are left. If the displaced holder has a command still in flight — a waited `move_joints` is the one that lasts — the hand-over gives up after 250 ms and the preemption is refused with 409 `hand-over timed out; the current holder has a command in flight`; the lease does not move. Stop the robot (`/v1/soft_kill`, `estop` — never leased) and ask again.

There is no push notification: a displaced holder finds out by reading `GET /v1/arm/lease` (different `holder`, different `epoch`) or by having its next gated POST refused.

The holder and the class are self-declared, not credentials: this daemon authenticates nobody, and the lease coordinates cooperating consumers rather than defending against a hostile one. Arbitration is opt-in — with no lease held every verb behaves exactly as it did before.

**The token.** This answer, for a fresh grant and for a renewal, carries `token`: 16 hexadecimal digits that no other view of the lease shows. A fresh grant draws a new one and a renewal keeps it. Every command on the shared-memory command path `arm_command.shm/1` carries it, and one whose token is not the live lease's is refused.

**The motion fence.** Ask with `"fenced": true` and the answer also carries `fence`, which starts at 1 on a fresh grant and is kept by a renewal (a renewal keeps a fenced grant fenced). Every `x-arm-lease` request of a fenced grant must then carry the grant's `lease_token` and the `fence` it is sent under; one that does not is refused with 409 `stale_authority`. `POST /v1/arm/lease/fence` raises the fence. A daemon that implements the fence always answers `fence` to a request that asked for `fenced`, so its absence tells a consumer the daemon does not fence motion.
post.summary: Take, renew or preempt the operator lease on both arms

delete.description: Releases only if `holder` matches the current holder; releasing somebody else's lease is refused with 409. Releasing when no lease is held succeeds, so a consumer shutting down need not know whether its own lease already expired.

BadGateway.description: A device or backend failed, or the requested capability is not available in this daemon's configuration.

BadRequest.description: The request was malformed, out of range, or refused by the motion guard.

Conflict.description: The device's soft-kill latch is engaged, a device or mode policy refused an otherwise valid command, or (`kind: stale`) a timestamped command was not newer than the newest one already accepted.

GatewayTimeout.description: A device operation exceeded its deadline. The command may still have taken effect: it is not safe to assume a timeout means nothing happened.

NotFound.description: No such route, or no such navigation goal, trajectory job or expression.

Unprocessable.description: The request is well formed but its values do not fit the addressed resource (`kind: unprocessable`): an openness outside [0, 1], a joint count other than the declared degrees of freedom, a joint target outside its limits, a timestamp too far ahead of the daemon clock, or a field the resource's driver does not take.

Advisory.description:
One suggestion about one device's current state.

Additive everywhere it appears: absent when the state earns none.

code.description: The stable word to branch on.

message.description: One sentence for a human, naming the state and the next step.

severity.description: How much attention this asks for.

oneOf.description:
The call that changes the state, when the next step IS a call.

Absent when it is not: a lift whose daemon was started without
`[slider] commissioning = true` is moved on by editing that file and
restarting, and there is no verb for that on purpose (the REST
surface is unauthenticated, so a verb that turned commissioning on
would be a verb that turned every other gate off). An advisory with
no action still names the step in `message`.

AdvisoryCode.description:
A stable machine word for one advisory, independent of its wording.

A consumer branches on this, never on [`Advisory::message`] — the same
rule [`crate::ErrorKind`] states for failures, for the same reason.

AdvisorySeverity.description:
How much of an operator's attention one advisory asks for.

An enum rather than a bare string so a later advisory can be published at
a higher severity without any consumer changing the shape it parses.
Today exactly one severity is produced: both the arm's idle state and the
lift's uncommissioned origin are states the machine is legitimately in,
so they are information and nothing more.

ApproachSlowing.description:
How a streamed `move_joints_both` tick was slowed. Present on the answer
only when the pose written differs from the pose sent.

cause.description: Whether the stream or the arm's own speed asked for it.

commanded_a.description: Arm A's written joint target, in degrees.

commanded_b.description: Arm B's written joint target, in degrees.

distance.description:
The clearance of that stage's binding pair at the written pose:
metres, or degrees to the limit for `joint_limit`.

scale_a.description:
The fraction of arm A's step, from the previous written target to the
sent one, that was written: `1` unchanged, `0` held.

oneOf.description:
The arm that stage belongs to; absent for `arm_arm` and `hand_arm`,
which are both.

stage.description: The stage that asked for the smallest scale.

stop.description:
The distance at which that stage allows no approach at all (the
guard's margin plus 0.1 mm, or the joint limit), in the same unit.

ApproachStage.description: The clearance stage a slowing came from.

ArmContractHeader.description: The 32-byte header every arm contract message starts with.

instance_id.description:
The daemon's instance: drawn once when it starts, so a consumer can
tell a restarted daemon from the one it was reading.

mono_ns.description: `CLOCK_MONOTONIC` nanoseconds when the daemon produced the message.

seq.description: Strictly increasing from 1 per contract since the daemon started.

ArmFeedbackRecord.description:
One controller feedback record, every signal of it: the
`arm_feedback.shm/1` message as JSON.

controller_version.description:
The controller's firmware version, `0` while the daemon has not read
it.

flags.description:
`FEEDBACK_*` bits: `1` the controller's firmware family contradicts
the configured protocol, `2` the raw record was truncated.

header.description:
The common header; `seq` counts the records since the daemon started,
`mono_ns` is when it produced this one.

layout_sha256.description:
The SHA-256 of the contract's committed layout document: which
version of the contract these fields are.

para_cmd_serial.description: The serial of the parameter command the reply slot belongs to.

para_name.description: The parameter reply's name (the wire's NUL-padded bytes, as text).

para_ret_serial.description:
The controller's return serial for that command: the serial, or
`error_code * 100 + serial` on a refusal.

para_type.description: The parameter reply's type (`0` int32, `1` float, `2` string).

protocol.description:
`PROTOCOL_*`: the host-to-controller wire generation the daemon
speaks (`0` unknown, `1` the first generation, `2` the second
generation).

raw.description: The record as received, `raw_len` bytes, base64.

raw_len.description: How many bytes of the record `raw` holds.

rx_mono_ns.description: `CLOCK_MONOTONIC` nanoseconds when the daemon received the record.

sides.description: Arm A (index 0, the physical left arm) and arm B (index 1).

ArmLease.description:
The published view of the lease, as `POST /v1/arm/lease`,
`GET /v1/arm/lease` and the `arm.lease` slot of `GET /v1/state` return it.

class.description:
The privilege class the holder claimed. A request of a strictly higher
class takes these arms away; an equal or lower one is refused.

epoch.description:
Monotonic grant counter, incremented on every FRESH grant and left
alone by a heartbeat renewal.

This is what tells a consumer that reads `holder == "me"` whether it
is the same grant it had a moment ago: an unchanged `epoch` means it
never lost the arms, while a higher one means it was displaced and
later granted them again — and therefore that whatever it believed
about the arms' pose, mode or tool registration is stale.

expires_in_s.description:
Whole seconds until the lease expires, rounded up. Once this reaches
zero the lease is gone: the next caller takes it without asking.

fence.description:
The grant's current motion fence: present only for a lease granted
`fenced`, absent otherwise.

It starts at 1 on a fresh fenced grant, is kept by a renewal and is
raised by `POST /v1/arm/lease/fence`. Its presence in the answer to a
request that asked for `fenced` is how a consumer knows that this
daemon fences motion.

holder.description: The self-declared name of the consumer holding the arms.

preempted_from.description:
The holder this lease was taken away from, when it was taken by
preemption rather than granted freely. `null` for an ordinary grant.

It survives renewals, because it describes how this grant came about
and that does not change when the holder heartbeats.

token.description:
The grant's token, 16 hexadecimal digits: present only in the answer
to the holder's own `POST /v1/arm/lease`, and absent from every other
view of the lease.

A fresh grant draws a new token and a renewal keeps it, exactly as it
keeps the epoch. Every command on the shared-memory command path
(`arm_command.shm/1`) carries it; one whose token is not the live
lease's is refused. Like the holder's name, it coordinates
cooperating consumers and is not a credential.

ttl_s.description: The TTL this lease was granted with, in seconds.

holder.description:
The holder releasing the lease. Releasing somebody else's lease is
refused with 409: a release is a consumer yielding, never a takeover.

ArmLeaseRequest.description: `POST /v1/arm/lease`: take, renew, or preempt the arm lease.

oneOf.description:
How privileged this request is: `ambient`, `policy` or `operator`.
**Omitted means `ambient`**, the lowest privilege there is.

That default is the whole reason this could ship without a flag day.
Every consumer that already speaks the lease sends no class, so on the
day the daemon is upgraded all of them rank lowest and nothing they do
changes: no existing caller is silently promoted into a position where
it can take the arms off a person. Privilege is something a consumer
opts into, one release at a time, as it is taught what it is — a
teleop station or a console claims `operator`, a learned policy claims
`policy`, and a consumer that needs neither stays correct exactly as
it is.

fenced.description:
Ask for a **fenced** grant: the answer then carries `fence`, and every
lease-arbitrated request of this grant must carry `lease_token` and
`fence` (see `POST /v1/arm/lease/fence`). Omitted or `false` is an
ordinary grant, arbitrated by name exactly as before.

A renewal keeps a fenced grant fenced whatever it sends; a renewal
that asks for `fenced` on an unfenced grant of the same holder fences
it from then on, starting at fence 1.

holder.description:
The consumer's own name, echoed back in every refusal so an operator
can see who to ask. Free-form, but use something a human can act on:
`vr-teleop`, `task-planner`, `console`.

ttl_s.description:
How long the lease should live, in seconds. Omitted means
[`DEFAULT_LEASE_TTL_S`]; the accepted range is `1..=600`. Re-POST with
the same holder to heartbeat.

ArmLimits.description:
The arm's joint travel, J1..J7 in SDK order, and both arms' HOME and STOW
poses.

home_deg.description:
Both arms' HOME pose in degrees: the kit's pose, embedded in the
daemon at build time. A consumer reads HOME here rather than keeping
angles of its own.

joints.description:
Per-joint travel, J1 first. Derived from the embedded `d1.urdf`, so it
is the same table the motion guard rejects against.

stow_deg.description:
Both arms' STOW (storage) pose in degrees: the kit's pose, compiled
into the daemon, arm B mirrored from arm A. A consumer reads STOW here
rather than keeping angles of its own, and drives the arms there with
`POST /v1/arm/stow_both`.

ArmModeCommand.description:
The advertised request body of `POST /v1/arm/{side}/mode`.

This is a *flattened, advertise-only* view of the tagged
[`d1fw_core::ArmModeRequest`] enum with the arm lease's optional `holder`
folded in as a top-level field. The daemon still deserializes the wire
body into `ArmModeRequest` and reads `holder` off it separately (see
`d1fw_front_rest::lease`); nothing deserializes into this struct. It exists
only so the published document describes the body as one flat object.

`openapi-python-client` silently skips any endpoint whose request body is
an `allOf` containing a `oneOf`, which is exactly what the tagged enum plus
a composed-in `holder` used to emit — so `POST /v1/arm/{side}/mode`, the
most-used arm verb, was missing from every generated Python client. A
single flat object with a `mode` string discriminator and every per-variant
parameter optional generates cleanly. Which fields are required for a given
`mode`, and their defaults, are documented on [`d1fw_core::ArmModeRequest`]
and enforced by the daemon, not by this looser schema.

acc_ratio.description:
Acceleration ratio, as a backend-defined normalized ratio
(`0.0..=1.0`). Used by the same four modes as `vel_ratio`.

adjustment_limit_mm.description:
`force_compliance`: how far, in millimetres, the controller may
displace the end effector to comply. Must be positive.

anchor_command_pose.description:
`force_compliance`: write the measured pose into the controller's
commanded pose before the transition. On by default, unsafe to disable.

control_params.description:
`force_compliance`: force-loop gains and limits; all zeros selects the
controller's built-in defaults.

damping.description:
Joint (`torque`) or Cartesian (`cartesian_impedance`) damping, seven
entries. Omitted requests the mode's own default.

eef_rotation.description:
`cartesian_impedance`: end-effector rotation parameters forwarded to
the controller.

force_direction.description:
`force_compliance`: which Cartesian directions (X, Y, Z, Rx, Ry, Rz)
the force loop acts on; `1` enables a direction, `0` disables it.

holder.description:
The arm lease holder issuing this command. Required only while somebody
holds the lease: with no lease held the field is ignored, and with one
held a request whose `holder` does not match is refused with 409.

mode.description: Which arm control mode to enter; selects which of the other fields apply.

stiffness.description:
Joint (`torque`) or Cartesian (`cartesian_impedance`) stiffness, seven
entries. Omitted requests the mode's own default.

target_force.description:
`force_compliance`: target contact force in newtons. Must not be
negative; any positive value is an active push, not a threshold.

vel_ratio.description:
Velocity ratio, as a backend-defined normalized ratio (`0.0..=1.0`).
Used by `position`, `torque`, `cartesian_impedance` and
`force_compliance`.

zero_wrist_roll.description:
`force_compliance`: command the wrist-roll joint (J7) to zero as part
of the entry anchor rather than freezing it in place.

ArmSide.description: Selects one of the two physical arms.

ArmSideFeedbackRecord.description:
One arm side of one controller feedback record: what the controller
reported for this side, in its own units and codes (`arm_feedback.shm/1`
`SideFeedback`).

acc_ratio.description: The joint acceleration ratio in effect, percent.

accepted_cmd.description: The newest host joint target the controller accepted, degrees.

cart_dn.description: The null-space damping of the redundant seventh joint.

cart_kd_type.description: The Cartesian stiffness/damping type in effect.

cart_kn.description: The null-space stiffness of the redundant seventh joint.

cmd_echo.description: The joint command the controller echoes on its output side, degrees.

cur_state.description:
The controller's current state code (`STATE_*`: 0 idle, 1 position,
2 PVT, 3 torque, 4 released, 100 error, 101-104 and 109 transitions).

current.description:
The per-joint current (commanded torque) the controller reports
(controller unit).

error_code.description: The controller's error code; `0` while it reports none.

est_cart_fn.description:
The controller's estimated Cartesian force/torque at the tool
(controller unit).

est_force.description: The controller's estimated external joint force (controller unit).

est_friction.description: The controller's estimated joint friction (controller unit).

force_adj_lmt.description: The compliance adjustment limit in effect, millimetres.

force_cmd.description: The force command in effect, newtons.

force_dir.description: The force-controlled Cartesian directions in effect.

force_pidul.description: The force loop's seven control parameters in effect.

frame_miss_count.description:
Host command frames the controller reckons it did not receive,
refreshed every 200 control cycles; healthy below 20.

imp_type.description: The selected impedance type: `1` joint, `2` Cartesian, `3` force.

in_frame_serial.description: The serial of the newest host command frame the controller took.

low_speed.description:
The controller's low-speed (stationary) flag: nonzero while the arm
is not moving.

max_frame_miss_count.description:
The high-water mark of `frame_miss_count` since the controller
started.

pos_e.description: The controller's per-joint position error (controller unit).

sys_cyc.description: The controller's own cycle counter, modulo 1 000 000.

sys_cyc_miss_count.description: Controller realtime cycles that missed their deadline.

tool_dyn.description:
The tool dynamics registered on the controller: mass (kg), centre of
mass (mm) and inertia.

tool_kine.description:
The tool kinematics registered on the controller: TCP translation
(millimetres) and rotation (degrees).

torque.description: The per-joint torque the joint sensors report, newton-metres.

vel.description: Measured joint velocities, degrees per second.

vel_ratio.description: The joint velocity ratio in effect, percent.

a.description: Arm A target joint angles in degrees, seven joints.

b.description: Arm B target joint angles in degrees, seven joints.

wait.description: Block until both arms report arrival (up to 30 s).

ChassisLimits.description: The mobile base's remote-drive ceilings and watchdog intervals.

cmd_vel_repeat_ms.description: How often a held velocity is repeated to the base, in ms.

deadman_ms.description: How long a velocity command stays live without a refresh, in ms.

omega.description: Angular velocity in radians per second; positive is counter-clockwise.

vx.description: Forward velocity in metres per second; negative is reverse.

DiagnosticIdentity.description:
Which daemon answered, carried beside the failure `GET /v1/health` gives on
a daemon started with `--diagnostic` (the failure envelope's
`diagnostic`). A consumer that only checks health sees a failure; one that
wants to know what answered reads this, then `GET /v1/components`.

commit.description:
The source commit the daemon was built from, or `null` when the build
was not told one.

uptime_s.description: Whole seconds since this frontend started serving.

EndEffector.description:
One side, as `GET /v1/end_effectors` and `GET /v1/end_effectors/{side}`
answer it.

available.description:
Whether a command on this side can reach its device now. `false`
for a side that carries nothing, a declared device that has not answered
its probe yet, and an out-of-process provider that
has not announced itself or has stopped sending its heartbeat; `error`
then says which.

oneOf.description: What the driver declares, or `null` for a side that carries nothing.

error.description: Why the state could not be read, when it could not.

fitted.description: Whether the configuration fits an end effector to this side.

last_joints_timestamp_us.description:
The newest `joints` timestamp accepted on this side, microseconds
since the Unix epoch, or `null` before the first one.

oneOf.description: The operator-entered product for this side, independent of its driver.

side.description:
The arm side the end effector is bolted to (`a` is the physical LEFT
arm).

oneOf.description: The newest state, or `null` when nothing is fitted or the read failed.

EndEffectorCapabilities.description:
What one end effector can do, so a client negotiates instead of
assuming. Every flag is a promise the driver keeps.

contact_sensing.description: The state reports whether the end effector stopped on an object.

force_sensing.description: How the force the end effector applies is sensed.

grip_presets.description:
The named grip presets `set` accepts in `grip`; empty when the driver
takes no grip.

joint_effort.description: The state reports each joint's actuator effort (`joint_efforts`).

joint_velocity.description: The state reports each joint's velocity (`joint_velocities`).

max_command_hz.description:
The vendor-rated ceiling on commands and polls together, in hertz,
when the vendor publishes one.

set_extra.description:
The keys `set` accepts in its driver-scoped `extra` object; empty when
the driver takes none. What each key means is the driver's to
document.

stroke_completion.description:
`set` with `wait: true` blocks until the driver's stroke concludes and
reports a stroke that did not complete as an error. Without it, `wait`
returns once the command is on the wire.

EndEffectorDescriptor.description:
What a driver declares about the end effector it drives. Decided by the
configuration and the probe; the one field that changes is `node_id`, from
`null` to the address a later probe found, once.

detail_schema.description:
The schema id (`"<id>/<major>"`) the state's `detail` follows, or
`null` when the driver publishes no detail. A consumer decides what
to read from a side by its `capabilities` and `joints`, and reads the
detail only for a schema id it knows.

driver.description: The driver name the side's provider declares, passed through unread.

guard_model.description:
The id of the arm-guard envelope this end effector declares, passed
through as the provider names it, or `null` when it declares none.

guard_model_applied.description:
The envelope the arm guard checks this side's end effector with:
`guard_model` when the guard has an envelope of that id, otherwise
the guard's default flange envelope (`"default"`). A value other than
`guard_model` means the guard fell back.

joints.description:
The joints of the `joints` command mode, in command order. Its length
is the end effector's degrees of freedom.

model.description: The model the side's provider declares, passed through unread.

node_id.description:
The bus address the probe found the device at, or `null` while
nothing has answered — every command on the side is then refused with
`unavailable`, and the side is probed again until its device answers.

oneOf.description:
The tool registration the daemon makes on this side's arm for this
end effector, in the values `POST /v1/arm/{side}/tool` takes, exactly
as the side's provider declares it; `null` when it declares none, and
the daemon then registers nothing for the side. A tool a client
registers outranks it until the daemon restarts.

EndEffectorDetail.description:
A driver's own report: opaque to everything but the consumers of its
schema.

`schema` identifies the schema `data` follows, as `"<id>/<major>"`
(for example `acme.report/1`). The id is owned by whoever produces
the report, an external provider included, and the major changes only
when the data changes incompatibly; a field added to the data keeps it.
A consumer reads `data` only for a schema id it knows.

schema.description:
The schema `data` follows, `"<id>/<major>"`; the same id the
descriptor's `detail_schema` declares.

EndEffectorJoint.description: One joint an end effector exposes to the `joints` command mode.

name.description: The joint's name, unique on this end effector.

unit.description: The unit targets and readings are in.

EndEffectorJointUnit.description: The unit one end-effector joint is commanded and reported in.

EndEffectorProduct.description: What the operator entered for one side's end effector.

model_number.description: The maker's model number as printed on the unit (`ACME-100`).

revision.description: The unit's revision (`V1.2`), a note only; `null` when not entered.

updated_at.description: When it was saved (UTC, RFC 3339), set by the daemon.

updated_by.description: Who saved it, `null` when not given.

EndEffectorSetRequest.description:
The body of `POST /v1/end_effectors/{side}/set`.

Unknown fields are refused rather than ignored: a client still sending the
retired gripper body's `closedness` (whose scale runs the other way), or a
driver-specific field outside `extra`, must hear about it, not have the
field dropped.

extra.description:
Driver-scoped parameters, only the keys the driver lists in its
capabilities' `set_extra` (422 otherwise). Their meaning is the
driver's own and is documented with the driver. The key
`force_percent` is such a key, taken by a driver that lists it; sent
with the request's own `force_percent`, the two must be equal (422
otherwise).

force_percent.description:
The grip force, `0` the gentlest the end effector can apply … `100`
its maximum, mapped linearly onto the end effector's own force range.
Every fitted end effector with openness takes it: one without
adjustable force applies its fixed force, and a side whose provider
does not take it has it dropped, which `state.grip_force` reports
(`mode`). Refused (422) when not finite, outside `[0, 100]`, or sent
with `grip` or `torque_nm`. Omitted, the grip is what `grip`,
`torque_nm`, `extra` or the driver's default makes it.

oneOf.description: A named grip preset, for a driver whose capabilities list it.

openness.description:
`0.0` fully closed … `1.0` fully open. For a gripper this is its one
openness degree of freedom; for a multi-finger hand `1.0` is an open
hand and `0.0` a fist. Outside `[0, 1]` the request is refused (422).

torque_nm.description:
An explicit grip cap in newton-metres, for a driver with
`grip_torque`.

wait.description:
Block until the stroke concludes (default `true`). With `false` the
call returns once the target is recorded, and a stroke gripper drives
toward the newest target in the background — the lane a fixed-rate
controller streams into.

EndEffectorState.description: One end effector's dynamic state, in vendor-neutral terms.

cap_reached.description:
Whether the newest closing stroke concluded at its force cap, when the
driver caps force.

contact.description:
Whether the newest closing stroke stopped on an object, when the
driver has contact sensing.

oneOf.description:
The driver's own report, for what the neutral fields above do not
carry, or `null` when the driver has none.

fault.description: The fault the device reports, or `null` when it reports none.

oneOf.description:
The grip force in effect and how it answers `force_percent`: the
report of a provider that takes `force_percent`, or `mode: not_taken`
for one that does not. `null` when the side's provider takes
`force_percent` but published no well-formed report, and for a driver
that does not report it. Always present in a daemon that takes
`force_percent`; an older daemon omits it.

holding.description: Whether the end effector holds an object, when it can tell.

joint_efforts.description:
The effort each joint's actuator reports, newton-metres for a rotary
actuator and newtons for a linear one: one entry per entry of
`joints`, `null` for a joint whose effort is not known, or empty when
the driver reports none (`capabilities.joint_effort`).

joint_velocities.description:
Measured joint velocities, in each joint's unit per second: one entry
per entry of `joints`, `null` for a joint whose velocity is not
known, or empty when the driver reports none
(`capabilities.joint_velocity`).

joints.description:
Measured joint positions in the descriptor's order and units; empty
when the driver has no reading.

live.description:
Whether the reading was taken for this call, or the newest one a
running command folded, rather than an older cached one.

openness.description:
The driver's estimate of the current openness (`0.0` closed … `1.0`
open), or `null` when it has no reading to estimate from.

torque_nm.description: The torque the actuator reports, newton-metres, when it reports one.

tracking.description: Whether a streamed target is being driven toward right now.

ErrorEnvelope.description: The failure envelope. `data` is always null; `message` always carries the daemon's own or the mobile base's error text; `kind` is always present and is the stable machine word to branch on; `code` is the mobile base's own numeric response code and is present only when the failure came from the base. Branch on `kind`, never on `message`. `advisory` is present only when the refusal knows the next step, and is absent otherwise. `diagnostic` is present only on the 503 of `GET /v1/health` from a daemon started with `--diagnostic`, and names which daemon answered.

code.description: The mobile base's numeric response code, or null when the failure did not come from the base.

ErrorEnvelope.title: ErrorEnvelope

ErrorKind.description:
A stable machine word for one failure, independent of its wording.

Every error this daemon returns carries one of these, and a consumer
branches on it rather than on the prose in `message`, which is the vendor's
or the daemon's own sentence and is free to change. The values fall into
two groups: the daemon's own conditions, and the mobile base's, which are
the vendor response codes classified into what an operator can do about
them.

ForceSensing.description: How an end effector senses the force it applies.

GripForce.description:
The grip force in effect on one side, and how it answers
`force_percent`.

applied_value.description:
The force setting in effect, in the device's native `unit`, or `null`
when it is not known.

approx_newtons.description:
The approximate grip force of the value in effect, newtons, when the
vendor's documentation gives a basis for it; otherwise `null`.

oneOf.description:
The approximate newtons at `range.min` and `range.max`, on the same
basis as `approx_newtons`; otherwise `null`.

mode.description:
Whether `force_percent` is mapped onto an adjustable force, met by a
fixed one, or not taken by the side's provider.

oneOf.description:
The native values `force_percent` `0` and `100` map to, in `unit`;
`null` unless `mode` is `adjustable`.

requested_percent.description:
The `force_percent` of the newest `set`, or `null` when the newest
`set` named none or no `set` has arrived yet.

unit.description:
The unit of `applied_value` and `range`: `percent_of_device_scale`,
`newton_metre`, `newton`, `milliampere`, `ampere` or
`permille_of_rated_current`. `null` exactly when both `applied_value`
and `range` are `null`, so an adjustable end effector reports its unit
and range before its first `set`.

GripForceMode.description: How a side's grip force answers `force_percent`.

GripForceRange.description: A closed interval of a grip-force quantity.

GripPreset.description:
A named grip a `set` may ask for.

The vocabulary is shared by every driver; what force each preset stands
for is the driver's own configuration, and a driver lists the presets it
takes in [`EndEffectorCapabilities::grip_presets`]. `firm` is what a
driver that takes presets applies when a stroke names none.

HomePose.description:
Both arms' HOME joint angles, degrees, SDK order J1..J7.

HOME is the kit's pose (manipulation-kit's `config/home_pose.json`,
embedded in the daemon at build time); the daemon never defines it a
second time.

a.description:
Arm A's HOME joint angles in degrees, J1 first (arm A is the physical
left arm).

b.description:
Arm B's HOME joint angles in degrees, J1 first (arm B is the physical
right arm).

JointLimit.description: One arm joint's travel, in degrees.

position.description: Target angle for that joint in degrees.

wait.description: Block until the arm reports arrival (up to 30 s).

joints_deg.description: Target joint angles in degrees, seven joints.

wait.description:
Block until the arm reports arrival (up to 30 s) rather than
returning as soon as the command is accepted.

LeaseClass.description:
How privileged one lease request is, and therefore what it may displace:
`ambient` (rank 10) < `policy` (50) < `operator` (90).

A request of a strictly higher class than the current holder preempts it;
an equal class is first-come and a lower one is refused. Three named
classes rather than a free integer, because a rank is only useful if two
consumers written by two people mean the same thing by it. The numeric
ranks are published for consumers whose own arbiter works in numbers, but
the wire form is always the name.

Limits.description: Every pinned envelope this daemon enforces, in one read.

arm.description: Arm joint travel and the HOME and STOW poses.

NeckCommand.description: A neck pose or pose-delta command.

pitch.description: Target or delta pitch in radians; positive is look-up.

relative.description: Interpret supplied axes as deltas when true.

velocity.description: Requested speed in radians per second.  `None` selects the core default.

yaw.description: Target or delta yaw in radians; positive is turn-right.

NeckLimits.description:
The neck's logical envelope, home pose and velocity ceilings.

LOGICAL frame throughout — the frame `neck/cmd` takes and `neck/state`
reports: pitch positive looks UP, yaw positive turns RIGHT. The motor frame
underneath (where the sign is inverted and the per-axis direction mapping
lives) is the backend's and is deliberately not published: nothing outside
this daemon writes a motor command, so a consumer that knew the motor frame
could only use it to get the mapping wrong.

default_velocity_rad_s.description: Velocity applied when a command names none, in radians/sec.

home_pitch_rad.description: Pitch of the home pose in radians.

home_yaw_rad.description: Yaw of the home pose in radians.

max_velocity_rad_s.description: Velocity ceiling a command is clamped to, in radians/sec.

pitch_max_rad.description: Highest commandable pitch in radians (looking up).

pitch_min_rad.description: Lowest commandable pitch in radians (looking down).

yaw_max_rad.description: Highest commandable yaw in radians (turned right).

yaw_min_rad.description: Lowest commandable yaw in radians (turned left).

NeckState.description: Neck feedback in the logical robot frame.

enabled.description: Whether the neck motors are enabled.

moving.description:
Whether either neck axis is moving.

The backend's own answer, taken from the same feedback frames as the
velocities beside it: an axis is moving when its measured velocity
exceeds what the motor's feedback can express, which is the wire's
resolution rather than a chosen threshold. A neck creeping below that
resolution reads `false`; nothing on this wire can tell it apart from
a standing motor. See [`crate::Motion`], which folds this into the
whole-robot answer.

pitch_coil_temperature_c.description:
The pitch motor's coil (winding) temperature in degrees Celsius;
`null` when the backend has none.

pitch_mos_temperature_c.description:
The pitch motor's MOSFET (drive) temperature in degrees Celsius, as
its status feedback reports it; `null` when the backend has none.

pitch_velocity.description: Current pitch velocity in radians per second.

yaw_coil_temperature_c.description:
The yaw motor's coil (winding) temperature in degrees Celsius; `null`
when the backend has none.

yaw_mos_temperature_c.description:
The yaw motor's MOSFET (drive) temperature in degrees Celsius; `null`
when the backend has none.

yaw_velocity.description: Current yaw velocity in radians per second.

SliderHardwareLimits.description:
The HARDWARE side of the torso lift's limits: what the drive itself holds
and acts on, every value read back from the drive.

The lift's constraints have two sides, kept under separate names because
they may legitimately hold different values and one is never derived from
the other. The SOFTWARE side is [`SliderTravelLimits`]
(`slider/state.travel_limits`): the ranges this daemon records and checks
a move against before anything reaches the drive. This is the other one:
on the D1's LD2-RS, the drive's own position limits — the positive limit
in `0x6006`:`0x6007` and the negative limit in `0x6008`:`0x6009`, signed
32-bit pulse counts measured from the drive's origin, in force while
`Pr8.00` (`0x6000`) bit 1 is set — and the two settings that decide
whether the drive keeps its origin across a power cycle. The vendor's
documentation calls the drive's limits "software limits" because the
drive's firmware enforces them rather than a limit switch; in this API
they are HARDWARE, because the drive holds and enforces them.

Read when the daemon connects to the drive and again after every daemon
write to them (`set_zero`, `set_hardware_limits`), and cached in between,
because they change only when written and the link runs at 9600 baud. A
field is `null` when the drive has not answered a reading of it. A
backend whose drive has no limit registers publishes
`limit_registers: false`; its hardware side is its origin alone.

limit_enabled.description:
HARDWARE: whether the drive's position limits are in force: `Pr8.00`
bit 1 as read from the drive. `set_zero` turns it off (the limits are
pulse counts from the origin it replaces); `set_hardware_limits`
turns it on.

limit_registers.description:
HARDWARE: whether this drive has position-limit registers the daemon
can write and read back. `true` for the D1's LD2-RS.

lower_m.description:
HARDWARE: the drive's negative position limit (`0x6008`:`0x6009`), in
metres from the drive's origin.

lower_pulses.description:
HARDWARE: the drive's negative position limit as the raw signed pulse
count it holds.

origin.description: HARDWARE: the drive's origin settings, as the drive holds them.

upper_m.description:
HARDWARE: the drive's positive position limit (`0x6006`:`0x6007`), in
metres from the drive's origin.

upper_pulses.description:
HARDWARE: the drive's positive position limit as the raw signed pulse
count it holds.

SliderHardwareOrigin.description:
The HARDWARE side's origin: the two drive settings that decide whether the
drive keeps the zero `set_zero` wrote across a power cycle.

abs_encoder_setting.description:
HARDWARE: `Pr0.15` (`0x001F`), the absolute-encoder setting, as read
from the drive. `1` is multi-turn absolute; `3` is the PR-only
zero-position-memory mode `set_zero` leaves the drive in.

position_memory.description:
HARDWARE: `Pr8.00` bit 3, absolute position memory, as read from the
drive: whether the position survives a power cycle.

min_height_m.description: Lower stop in metres; the origin heights are measured from.

travel_pulses.description: The whole stroke in drive pulses.

SliderMove.description:
A requested slider move: one absolute height, or one small relative
amount.

Exactly one of `height_m` and `delta_m` is given. Neither and both are
both rejected with `400` rather than resolved by a precedence rule: a
caller that sent two targets did not mean one of them, and a caller that
sent none named no move at all.

`delta_m` is the commissioning form. It is admitted only on a daemon
started with `[slider] commissioning = true`, it is capped at
[`crate::safety::SLIDER_COMMISSIONING_STEP_MAX_M`] per call, and it runs
at the commissioning floor
[`crate::safety::SLIDER_COMMISSIONING_SPEED_RATIO`] unless `speed_ratio`
names a speed at or above that floor (a lower one is `400`). It is on
this verb rather than on a new one because on the LD2-RS's wire the two
are the same PR path write with a different mode word (`0x0041` instead
of `0x0001`), so a separate verb would have been a second name for one
operation.

delta_m.description:
A small relative amount in metres, measured from where the carriage
stands now; negative is down. Commissioning only.

height_m.description:
Absolute target height in metres, measured from the drive's origin.

Optional in the schema only because `delta_m` is the alternative; a
body carrying neither is refused.

speed_ratio.description:
Optional move speed as a normalized ratio in `0.0..=1.0`: a fraction of
the slider's full speed, the same convention the arm's `vel_ratio`
uses (a fraction of full speed, never a percentage). `None` (the field
absent from the request body) keeps the backend's default speed, so an
existing caller is unchanged. Out-of-range values are rejected with
`400`. With `delta_m` it is the commissioning step's speed: absent, the
step runs at the commissioning floor (`0.05`); present, it must be at or
above that floor, and a lower value is rejected with `400` rather than
raised to it.

wait.description: Wait for the backend to report completion when true.

SliderMultiturnRecovery.description:
What the drive's multi-turn initialisation (`Pr0.15 := 9`) read, before
and after it: the answer of `recover_multiturn`, and part of the answer
of a `set_zero` that ran it.

Er153 (alarm `0x153`, decimal 339) is the LD2-RS7015's multi-turn encoder
battery error: the absolute position is lost. A drive taken into
multi-turn absolute mode without this initialisation shows Er153 at its
next power-up. The drive vendor's procedure runs it only on a drive in
Er153, never as a routine part of a zero; `set_zero` runs it there and
also on a new drive right after taking it from incremental mode into
absolute mode for the first time (such a drive cannot show Er153 before
its first power cycle in absolute mode), and `recover_multiturn` runs
it alone on a drive in Er153. It follows the
drive vendor's procedure for this drive: stop
(`0x6002 = 0x0040`), servo off (`0x0405 = 3`), the carriage confirmed
still, `0x001F = 9`, and within about 3 s `0x001F` back at `1` by itself
and `0x2203` reading 0. The initialisation does not make the position 0
(only the multi-turn count is cleared), so both positions are published;
the old coordinate is not trusted afterwards and nothing is derived from
it.

abs_encoder_setting_after.description:
`Pr0.15` (`0x001F`) as read when the initialisation completed: `1`,
the value the drive puts back by itself.

alarm_code_after.description:
The alarm register, masked to 12 bits, when the initialisation
completed: `0`.

alarm_code_before.description:
The alarm register (`0x2203`), masked to 12 bits, when the
initialisation began: `0x153` (339) on a drive in Er153, `0` on a new
drive `set_zero` took into absolute mode.

position_after_pulses.description:
The position in pulses where the carriage rested after the
initialisation. Not 0: the initialisation keeps the single-turn part.

position_before_pulses.description:
The position (`0x602C`:`0x602D`) in pulses where the carriage rested
after the stop and the servo-off, before the initialisation.

returned_after_ms.description:
Milliseconds from the `0x001F = 9` write to the read that found
`0x001F = 1` and no alarm.

abs_encoder_setting.description:
The raw `Pr0.15` absolute-encoder setting the decision was made from,
or `null` when the drive has not answered a reading of it. `1`
(multi-turn absolute enabled) is commissioned; `3` (clear
position-memory mode, where `set_zero` leaves a drive without
multi-turn absolute) is commissioned when `pr_control_setting` has
bit 3 set; anything else is not.

Published because `zero_reference: "unknown"` is otherwise a verdict
with no evidence: this field, `pr_control_setting` and `height_m` are
the readings that produced it.

oneOf.description:
An INFO-level suggestion about the origin above, when it earns one.

Additive and absent when it does not, so a consumer that has never
heard of it reads exactly the state it always read. A commissioned
and verified lift never carries one. See [`crate::slider_advisory`].

alarm.description:
Whether the slider reports an alarm (the drive's current-alarm
register `0x2203` is non-zero).

A carriage driven into its mechanical bottom stalls: the drive raises
an alarm, stops, and takes no further motion until the alarm is
cleared with `POST /v1/slider/reset_alarm`. Which code the D1's LD2-RS
raises for that stall has not been recorded on a robot; read it from
`alarm_code` and `alarm_text` rather than assuming one.

alarm_code.description:
The masked 12-bit raw alarm register value (see
`d1fw_proto_slider::AlarmCode`). `0` when the drive reports no alarm,
and also `0` when `comms_ok` is false since a failed read carries no
trustworthy register content.

availability_reason.description: The bring-up error while `available` is `false`; `null` otherwise.

available.description:
Whether the daemon has the lift at all.

`false` means the lift controller could not be brought up when the
daemon started (serial device missing, no answer, a frame that would
not parse): every lift verb then refuses with `kind: unavailable`, the
rest of the robot is served as usual, and the daemon keeps retrying in
the background — this flips to `true` without a restart once the lift
answers. `comms_ok` is then `false` too, and `availability_reason`
carries the error. Distinct from `comms_ok: false` with `available:
true`, which is a lift that is up but whose last reading failed.

comms_ok.description: Whether communications with the slider are healthy.

hardware_limits.description:
The HARDWARE side of the lift's limits: the drive's own position
limits and origin settings, read back from the drive. See
[`SliderHardwareLimits`]. Filled by the backend, which is the only
thing that can read the drive.

multiturn_lost.description:
Whether the drive's alarm is Er153 (`alarm_code` `0x153`, decimal
339): the multi-turn encoder's battery error, absolute position lost.

`reset_alarm` does not clear it. `POST /v1/slider/recover_multiturn`
recovers it, and so does `POST /v1/slider/set_zero`, whose first part
on such a drive is the drive vendor's multi-turn initialisation
(`Pr0.15 := 9`), before it sets the zero where the carriage stands;
every other alarm still refuses `set_zero`.

oneOf.description:
What `set_zero` read during its multi-turn initialisation, present
only in the answer of a `set_zero` that ran one: on a drive in Er153,
or on a new drive it took into absolute mode for the first time. See
[`SliderMultiturnRecovery`]. Absent from every other state.

pr_control_setting.description:
The raw `Pr8.00` PR control settings (register `0x6000`), or `null`
when the drive has not answered a reading of it. Bit 3 is absolute
position memory (the position survives a power cycle), bit 2 homing at
power-on, bit 1 the drive's own position limits (the HARDWARE side,
`hardware_limits`; the vendor's documentation calls them "software
limits" because the drive's firmware enforces them).

travel_limits.description:
The SOFTWARE side of the lift's limits: every range this daemon
records and enforces, and the range they come to together — the one
`set_height` admits. The drive's own limits are `hardware_limits`.

Additive to `travel_max_m`, which is unchanged and still the model
ceiling: `travel_limits.model.upper_m` is the same number. A console
that reads only `travel_max_m` keeps working and simply does not know
about a unit calibration narrower than the model.

Like `zero_verification` and `advisory`, this is filled where the
daemon hands the state out ([`crate::D1::slider_state`] and the
`/v1/state` snapshot) rather than by the backend: the unit layer
lives in the daemon's own state file, which no device can read. A
state taken straight from a device therefore carries the model layer
alone.

travel_max_m.description:
SOFTWARE side: the upper bound of the model travel in metres, the
highest `height_m` a move may target. Sourced from the daemon's `[slider]
travel_max_m` configuration (default `0.30` on a D1) so a console can
present the real limit instead of hardcoding one. The lower bound is
always `0.0` (the homed position), so no separate minimum is
published. Carried even when `comms_ok` is false, since it is a
configured fact rather than a live reading.

zero_reference.description:
Whether the drive's zero is plausibly the commissioned one. `unknown`
means `set_height` and `home` are refused with `409` until the
commissioning procedure has been run — see [`ZeroReference`].

zero_verification.description:
Whether the origin this daemon last wrote has been read back across a
power cycle. See [`ZeroVerification`].

SliderTravelLimits.description:
The SOFTWARE side of the torso lift's limits: every range this daemon
records and enforces itself, before anything reaches the drive, and what
they come to together. The drive's own limits are the HARDWARE side,
[`SliderHardwareLimits`], kept apart because the two may legitimately hold
different values.

The layers exist because "how high can this lift go" has more than one
answer and an operator needs to know WHICH one stopped a move. The model
ceiling is what a D1's lift is; the unit calibration is what this
particular machine's jig, cabling and mechanical build turned out to
allow, measured on a bench and recorded in the daemon's state file.

A layer only ever NARROWS: a unit calibration that claimed more travel
than the model has is refused when it is recorded, so `effective` can
never be wider than `model`.

effective.description:
SOFTWARE: the intersection of every layer above: the range the daemon
enforces on `set_height` and `home`, by direction (see
[`SliderTravelRange::admits_move`]).

model.description:
SOFTWARE: what the model allows, `[0, travel_max_m]` from `[slider]
travel_max_m` in the daemon's configuration.

oneOf.description:
SOFTWARE: the range `POST /v1/slider/set_limits` recorded for this
robot in the daemon's state file, or `null` when none has been
recorded.

SliderTravelRange.description: One closed interval of lift travel in metres.

lower_m.description: The lowest height this layer admits.

upper_m.description: The highest height this layer admits.

StowPose.description:
Both arms' STOW joint angles, degrees, SDK order J1..J7.

STOW is the storage pose: an endpoint the arms are parked in, not a
gesture. It is the manipulation-kit's pose at commit `ce802ad`; the
straight joint-space path from HOME to STOW was guard-clean in 101 of 101
runs. Arm B is arm A mirrored (J1, J3, J5 and J7 change sign).

a.description:
Arm A's STOW joint angles in degrees, J1 first (arm A is the physical
left arm).

b.description:
Arm B's STOW joint angles in degrees, J1 first (arm B is the physical
right arm): arm A's angles mirrored.

SuggestedAction.description:
The one call an advisory suggests, as a frontend-independent verb and
path.

The REST route is what is published because it is the one form every
frontend can be derived from: the WebSocket method for an arm's recover
path is `arm.{side}.recover`, and the mapping between the two is already
[`crate::API_MAP`].

path.description: The REST path, with any side already substituted.

ToolConfig.description: Tool-center-point and dynamics configuration for one arm.

com_mm.description: Centre of mass in millimetres, XYZ.

inertia.description: Inertia tensor components in the backend's six-value order.

WsRequest.description: One request frame sent by a WebSocket client.

id.description:
Caller-chosen correlation identifier, echoed in the response.

Responses can arrive out of order (see [`WsResponse`]), so this is the
only way to match a response to its request.

method.description:
The `x-ws-method` value of the operation to call, for example
`arm.a.move_joints`.  Side-templated operations are spelled with a
concrete side: `arm.a.mode`, never `arm.{side}.mode`.

params.description: The operation's request body, as an object.  Omitted means `{}`.

WsResponse.description:
One response frame, carrying the same payload the REST envelope would.

**Responses are not ordered.**  Each request is dispatched on its own
task, so a long motion call never delays another request on the same
connection and a later request can answer first.  Correlate by `id`, never
by arrival order.

code.description:
The mobile base's own numeric response code, when the failure came
from the base. Null on a failure raised by the daemon itself, and
absent from a success frame, which carries the three fields it has
always carried.

The same field the REST failure envelope carries, so a consumer that
speaks both frontends branches on one vocabulary.

data.description:
The operation's result on success, null on error.  This is the same
payload as the REST envelope's `data` for the same method.

oneOf.description:
Which daemon answered; the same object the REST failure envelope
carries. Present only on the failure frame of `health` from a daemon
started with `--diagnostic`, and absent from every other frame.

id.description:
The `id` of the request this answers, or null when the frame could not
be parsed far enough to recover one.

oneOf.description:
The stable machine word for the failure; absent from a success frame.

Branch on this rather than on `message`, which is the daemon's or the
mobile base's own sentence and is free to change.

message.description: The failure reason on error, null on success.

oneOf.description:
How the approach limiter slowed a streamed `arm.move_joints_both`;
the same object the REST success envelope carries. Present only on
a success frame of that method whose written pose is not the pose
sent, and absent from every other frame.

ZeroReference.description:
Whether the torso lift's drive origin is the one it was commissioned with.

The LD2-RS keeps its zero in the absolute encoder, and every height this
daemon accepts is measured from it. A drive that has lost that zero — a new
drive, an EEPROM that did not survive, a swapped motor — still answers
every register read: it simply calls some other place "0 m". A move to 0 m
against such an origin drives the lift into its mechanical stop.

So the origin is a published fact rather than an assumption, decided from
two readings the drive itself supplies: `Pr0.15` (the absolute-encoder
setting, which must be "multi-turn absolute enabled") and the current
position, which on a commissioned drive has to lie inside the usable
travel. See `d1fw_backends::slider::zero_reference`.

ZeroVerification.description:
Whether a zero that was written has been proved to have survived a power
cycle.

Separate from [`ZeroReference`] on purpose, and additive to it: the two
answer different questions and a consumer that only knows the older one
keeps reading exactly what it read. `zero_reference` asks "can the drive
vouch for its origin right now", which is decided from live readings.
This asks "has the origin this daemon last wrote been read back after the
power was removed", which no live reading can answer — it is a fact about
history, so it lives in the daemon's state file.

It matters because the LD2-RS reports its EEPROM save as taken (`0x5555`)
before anything has proved the parameter is still there after power is
removed, and an origin that lived in RAM only is precisely the failure
`set_zero` exists to prevent.
